chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said to his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah: O my son,
I fear lest destitution overtakes you. So, seek Allāh’s protection from it, because destitution is deficiency of religious belief, perplexity of intelligence, and it is conducive to hatred.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and intellectual harms of poverty according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this profound advice to his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies poverty not merely as material lack but as a spiritual and intellectual impediment that compromises religious observance and mental clarity. This perspective is deeply rooted in Shia tradition, where the 'defect in religion' (manqasatun li'd-din) refers to the distraction and humility required by need, while the 'confusion of intellect' (madhashatun li'l-'aql) highlights how scarcity can cloud judgment and lead to moral compromise.
